chunks: From him, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun, from Abdullah ibn al-Rahman, from Mismar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who made the divorce of his wife in the hand of two men, so one of them divorced her and the other refused, so Imam Ali (peace be upon him) did not approve of that until they both agree on the divorce.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on divorce if two appointed agents disagree?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the condition of joint consensus in delegated divorce (*wakalah*), ruling that if one agent pronounces the divorce while the other refuses, the act is not valid until both agree. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the integrity of agency and the requirement for unified execution when multiple agents are appointed, preventing unilateral actions that might contradict the principal's intent. The ruling underscores the precision required in marital contracts to ensure the divorce is legally binding and complete.
